formal_evidence: Three independent per-run completion.json receipts, checked against saved plans, completed training events, held-out question IDs, predictions and native scores. A receipt check, not a rerun.
native_score_structure: scores.json maps each question ID to a score record and a question/answer/prediction record. results.txt reports the original mean (0-5), normalized mean (0-100) and sample count. All three fields were checked in every cell.
coverage_definition: After task i each run evaluated the first i domains in task_order, once each. All 108 cells had 1000 distinct question IDs matching the planned held-out questions, predictions and native judgments. These are repeated evaluations, not 108000 unique examples.
score_verification: For every cell the scorer inputs matched the predictions. The mean of the native judgments and its 0-100 normalization (20 times the mean) matched results.txt, and the normalized mean and denominator matched the run receipt. No scores are published.
execution_profile: Saved sample plans used four workers, batch size one and 16 accumulation steps. Completed LoRA-FT and PCLR training commands matched. Completed Octopus training commands used two workers and 32 accumulation steps; the effective batch remained 64. Stage counts describe logical plan commands, not retries or parallel workers.
limitations: status.json records bounded train/save/reload/infer/score probes for both backbones, not eight-task results. Both MR-LoRA pairs have diagnostic branch evidence only; the other 32 are marked task2_completed.

Temporary-checkpoint acceptance is not a durable recovery guarantee. Nine save fields say passed_temporary; Video-LLaVA DGG says passed for save but lacks a persistently retained native optimizer recovery checkpoint.
The per-target formal labels in status.json are stale for the three completed runs. Formal coverage comes from their individual completion receipts, not the bounded status table.
No full-mode or VideoLLaMA2 formal result is established here. These historical sample scores do not attest release-code identity, current judge availability, retained checkpoints or reproducibility.
